_comment: ASCEND restricted knowledge pack. Public reference data (MITRE ATT&CK, CWE, CAPEC, NVD/CVE) for ONLY the seven in-scope techniques and the two anchor CVEs, per docs/05 section 5 ('restrict the import to the neighbourhood of our seven techniques'). Transcribed offline so the lab network needs no internet route (docs/02 section 6). The Semester-1 knowledge_graph/ module replaces this file with a live restricted pull from the official feeds; the lookup interface stays the same.
_source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v14, MITRE CWE v4.13, MITRE CAPEC v3.9, NVD CVE records

T1548.001.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
T1548.001.description_text: Adversaries may abuse setuid or setgid bits to run a binary with the privileges of its owner. A binary owned by root with the setuid bit set, and with a documented shell escape, allows any user who can execute it to obtain a root shell.

T1548.003.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
T1548.003.description_text: Adversaries may abuse an over-permissive sudo configuration to execute commands as root. A NOPASSWD rule naming a binary with a shell escape (tar, find, vim, awk, python) is equivalent to granting an unauthenticated root shell to that account.

T1068.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
T1068.description_text: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability in the kernel or a privileged component to elevate from an unprivileged local account to root.

T1611.name: Escape to Host
T1611.description_text: Adversaries may break out of a container to gain access to the underlying host. A mounted Docker socket, or membership of the docker group, is root-equivalent on the host because it permits launching a privileged container.

T1021.004.name: Remote Services: SSH
T1021.004.description_text: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a remote machine over SSH and execute commands as that account.

T1550.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
T1550.description_text: Adversaries may reuse stolen authentication material, such as an SSH private key, to authenticate to systems other than the one it was taken from. A key accepted by more than one host multiplies the reach of a single disclosure.

T1552.001.name: Unsecured Credentials in Files
T1552.001.description_text: Adversaries may search local file systems for credentials stored insecurely: private keys, .env files, shell history and configuration files that are readable by accounts other than their owner.

T1021.004+T1550.name: Remote Services: SSH (reused credential)
T1021.004+T1550.description_text: Composite edge emitted by the path enumerator: an SSH login (T1021.004) performed with authentication material harvested elsewhere (T1550). ASCEND reports it as one edge because a reviewer reads it as one attacker action.

CVE-2022-0847.name: DirtyPipe
CVE-2022-0847.description: Uninitialised pipe_buffer.flags in the Linux kernel allows an unprivileged local user to overwrite data in arbitrary read-only files, including /etc/passwd, yielding root.

CVE-2021-4034.name: PwnKit
CVE-2021-4034.description: Out-of-bounds write in polkit's pkexec allows any unprivileged local user to gain full root privileges with no authentication.
